    Fail-safe N

    Source: R/meta-bias.R
    meta_failsafe.Rd

    meta_failsafe() computes the number of unpublished null studies needed to overturn a conclusion. type = "rosenthal" uses Stouffer's method (Rosenthal, 1979) with a one-sided level alpha; "orwin" finds the number of studies with effect zero that would shrink the inverse variance weighted mean to target (Orwin, 1983); "rosenberg" finds the number that would make the common-effect estimate non-significant at two-sided level alpha (Rosenberg, 2005).

    Usage

    meta_failsafe(
  .data,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  type = c("rosenthal", "orwin", "rosenberg"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  target = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, <meta_es> or <meta_fit> from meta_pool().

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    type

    "rosenthal", "orwin" or "rosenberg".

    alpha

    Significance level.

    target

    Target effect for type = "orwin". Defaults to half the observed mean.

    Value

    A one row tibble with the method, the fail-safe number (fail_safe_n), the observed estimate (for Orwin and Rosenberg), target, alpha and the p.value of the observed evidence.

    References

    Rosenthal, R. (1979). The file drawer problem and tolerance for null results. Psychological Bulletin, 86(3), 638-641. doi:10.1037/0033-2909.86.3.638

    Orwin, R. G. (1983). A fail-safe N for effect size in meta-analysis. Journal of Educational Statistics, 8(2), 157-159. doi:10.3102/10769986008002157

    Rosenberg, M. S. (2005). The file-drawer problem revisited: a general weighted method for calculating fail-safe numbers in meta-analysis. Evolution, 59(2), 464-468. doi:10.1111/j.0014-3820.2005.tb01004.x

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
meta_failsafe(bcg)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   type      fail_safe_n estimate target alpha  p.value
#>   <chr>           <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 rosenthal         598       NA     NA  0.05 8.81e-30
meta_failsafe(bcg, type = "orwin", target = log(0.9))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   type  fail_safe_n estimate target alpha p.value
#>   <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 orwin          41   -0.430 -0.105  0.05      NA
